note: Acceptable/best indices are intentionally empty. The reviewed fixture is committed separately after a person inspects every sheet.

cases.ambiguity: A click on the flank also matches the head/legs; candidates disagree between whole-body and part masks.
cases.annotationNotes: Three near-identical whole-animal masks; #1 (score 0.700, 7.5% area) is a noisy partial that covers the rear body and fills the trunk curl. Provider top-1 (#3) is correct.

cases.ambiguity: Part intent with a negative correction on the body; the model may still return the whole animal.
cases.annotationNotes: Provider top-1 (#3, score 0.963) is a full-width vegetation band; #0 and #2 are vegetation too. Only #1 (score 0.807, 2.8% area) is localized on the head/trunk. This is a ranking failure with an acceptable candidate available, not a generation failure.

cases.ambiguity: Hair and backdrop share a boundary; candidates can split at the braid, at the hairline, or return the studio backdrop.
cases.annotationNotes: Three hair masks differing at the crown and bun (#1 has a small detached bun speckle and the highest score); #3 is the studio backdrop oval with the head punched out. Provider top-1 (#1) is correct.

cases.ambiguity: The click lands on the eye, so the correct answer depends on intent. This case declares whole-animal intent and shares its prompt with the eye case.
cases.annotationNotes: The whole animal exists as #3 (score 0.931, 15.8% area). The top-scoring candidates (#1 0.980, #0 0.739) are eye/part masks at the click; #2 (2.1%) is a claw/leg part. Candidate generation is adequate; the ranking picks a part, so top-1 is unacceptable for whole-animal intent.

cases.ambiguity: Same click as the whole-crab case, part intent: the tiny masks a precise click produces are correct here, not a failure.
cases.annotationNotes: Identical candidate set to crab-subject-whole; only the declared intent differs. The eye-scale masks (#0, #1) are correct here and #2/#3 are not. Provider top-1 (#1) is correct for this intent. This pair exists to prove ranking metrics must be intent-specific.

cases.intent: the mineral terrace under the click
cases.ambiguity: The click sits on the boundary between the thin blue water strip and the orange mineral crust. A declared intent is required: the crust is one candidate set, the water strip is another. Intent determines which is acceptable.
cases.annotationNotes: The three terrace masks agree at 54-56% area (scores 0.787 / 0.943 / 0.956); #1 (4.3%) is the thin blue water strip, a different object under this declared intent. Provider top-1 (#3) is correct.

reviewedBy: maintainer visual review of the per-case contact sheets
reviewMethod: For each case the source, every candidate mask (binary sheet), and the prompt markers were inspected as rendered PNGs; acceptable/best indices were decided from those images plus per-candidate area and bounding-box statistics. No IoU is recorded because the corpus has no pixel ground truth: it is an intent-annotation set.
promptNote: crab-subject-whole and crab-subject-eye share one prompt on purpose: they are the independent acceptable-alternative annotations for an inherently ambiguous click.
baselineNote: Recorded from the first reviewed run of this corpus (2026-09-15). These are floors, not targets: the test fails if top-1 acceptance falls below them. top1MatchesBest at the same run: provider 0/6, score 4/6, guarded-band-box 3/6, guarded-band-area 2/6.
